q: How does Token-2022 round a transfer fee?
f: Token-2022 computes the fee as ceil(amount × basis points ÷ 10,000), capped at the maximum fee. For 401 base units at 25 bps the program expects 2, not 1. A reader caught the Lab rounding it down, and the formula was fixed on November 9, 2026 with new tests.

q: Does the Required Memo rule check that an invoice number is right?
bold: No, only that a memo exists.
f: Token-2022 rejects a transfer without a memo, but it never reads the text: a payment marked with a wrong invoice number still passes on-chain. Wen Open Lab now matches the invoice off-chain at reconciliation and tests both the right and the wrong case.

q: What status can a reader's finding get in Wen Open Lab?
bold: Fixed, Known limit or Not an issue.
f: Every question a reader raises gets one answer that cites a test anyone can run with npm test, an honest status with the reason, and credit to the reader. Nothing is deleted: old answers stay with the date they changed.

q: Which token program owns the WEN mint, read on-chain on November 11, 2026?
f: An open check read the mint at slot 468049071: owner program TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA, the original SPL Token program, with no extensions.

q: How is WEN connected to Token-2022?
f: The poem behind WEN was minted as an NFT with WNS, a standard on Token-2022; the trillion fungible WEN tokens live on the original SPL Token program.

q: Can the WEN token charge a transfer fee?
f: The original SPL Token program cannot carry extensions, so a transfer fee cannot exist on WEN; the mint and freeze authorities are also revoked. What you pay is the Solana network fee and, on a swap, the pool fee your wallet shows before you sign.

q: In the January 5, 2024 poll, what share voted to test the new launch site with a meme coin?
f: Meow asked whether to test the JUP launch site with a meme coin first; 83.5% of 14,581 votes said yes. That test became WEN.

q: At launch, how many NFTs had been minted on the WNS standard?
f: The launch-eve thread from the Ovols side described the poem as the first and only NFT on WNS at the time.

q: What can Wen Counter, the Lab's point of sale, do with a shop's money?
f: Wen Counter is receive-only by design: no wallet connection, no signing, no keys, and only three read requests in code. Refunds are made inside the shop's own wallet.

q: Is the Wen cat a separate project from the WEN token?
bold: No, it is WEN's own face.
f: The Wen cat is the brand identity of WEN, the coin that was the first real-world use of WNS. The cat theme runs from the mascot to the creator's handle, Meow.

q: Which features can Token-2022 add to a token without third-party programs?
f: Transfer fees, transfer hooks, confidential transfers, interest-bearing tokens, permanent delegate, non-transferable tokens, metadata and metadata pointer, and group and member pointers, all set at the mint or account level.

q: Which Token-2022 extensions did the poem NFT behind WEN carry?
bold: Metadata pointer, group and member, transfer hook.
f: The poem was minted with WNS, so the NFT itself carried Token-2022 extensions; it was then split into one trillion WEN on the original SPL Token program, which is why WEN moves like an ordinary SPL token.

q: How can a transfer hook help tokenized real-world assets?
bold: The rules travel inside the transfer.
f: With Token-2022 transfer hooks, checks such as KYC or geo-restrictions can run on every transfer of the token itself, a requirement for regulated financial instruments.

q: Which Ethereum standards try to do what Token-2022 does natively?
f: On Ethereum, rules for security tokens are added as extra standards; on Solana, Token-2022 makes such controls a native part of the token program.

q: What does the Lab's warranty card keep on-chain about the order?
bold: A SHA-256 hash of the order.
f: The chain stores only a hash; the buyer keeps the order and can prove the match later, with no personal data on a public ledger.

q: In the Lab's invoice token, why does every new account start frozen?
bold: The issuer approves each counterparty first.
f: Default Account State = Frozen: only accounts the issuer thaws after its own checks can send or receive.

q: Besides the hook's program, what should a buyer read from an NFT's transfer hook?
f: The program is today's rule; the authority decides who can point the hook somewhere else tomorrow.

q: With Solana Pay, how does a shop find the payment for one order?
f: Each order gets a fresh reference key; the wallet adds it to the transfer, so the shop can find that payment on-chain.

q: What does LiteSVM do in Wen Open Lab's tests?
bold: Runs Solana programs locally, with no network.
f: LiteSVM loads the real Token-2022 and Memo programs into the test process, so the Lab's checks run in milliseconds, offline.

q: In the Lab's fee simulator example, where does almost all of the on-chain cost sit?
bold: In converting tokens to local money.
f: In the example the network part is 0.02 SOL for 2,000 payments a month, while a 0.5% conversion comes to $400.

q: Why does the Lab's receipt remove its mint authority after minting one token?
bold: So a second copy can never be minted.
f: Zero decimals, supply 1 and no mint authority make a true one-of-one, the light-NFT layout WNS uses.

q: Anyone can copy a token's name, ticker and logo. What can't be copied?
f: The address is identity. The real WEN is WENWENvqqNya429ubCdR81ZmD69brwQaaBYY6p3LCpk: search the address, not the name.

q: Which Token-2022 extension lets one key move or burn tokens from any holder?
f: The Lab's token inspector flags it in plain words, so a holder knows the powers behind a token before receiving it.

q: Why must a shop call validateTransfer after findReference?
f: findReference only says a transaction mentions the key; validateTransfer checks the recipient, amount, token, reference and memo.

q: In Wen Counter, what is the shop's identity?
f: The shop pastes its wallet's public receiving address; the counter checks it on-chain at setup and shows it on every QR screen.

q: With a card fee of 2.9% + 0.30, what share of a 3-dollar ice cream goes to the card fee?
f: 0.087 plus 0.30 is 0.387, or 12.9% of 3. The fixed part makes small tickets the most expensive: the micro-ticket effect.

q: How much does Wen Counter cost a shop?
f: The counter is free and open (Apache-2.0) and takes no fee per sale; the only on-chain cost of a sale is the Solana network fee, paid by the buyer's wallet.

q: Who pays the Solana network fee when a buyer pays a shop through Wen Counter?
f: The signer pays the fee: 5,000 lamports per signature, half burned and half to the validator. The shop receives the full amount.
